source.original_title: 05/08/2026 - Clive Abrahams & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/08/2026 - Clive Abrahams & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Follow Up

rep.name: Harry Edmonds
rep.location: Nomadic — in England at time of call; states he normally lives between Mexico and Colombia

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: I know you spoke with Kim. He gave me like a little bit of an overview. So I've kind of got a head start on you.

prospect.name: Clive Abrahams
prospect.location: Wirksworth, near Derby, Peak District, UK; South African, previously 11 years in Dubai
prospect.occupation: Senior corporate role with regional responsibility for the Middle East; relocated to the UK to take over a retiring colleague's position. Sedentary — eight to nine hours a day seated on calls.
prospect.family_status: Married; relocated to the UK with his wife roughly two years ago
prospect.training_background: Thirty years of cycling as his primary sport, plus supporting gym work and yoga. Rode at 74kg in Dubai; his stated ideal riding weight is 70-75kg. Essentially inactive for the last two years since relocating — bikes and TRX are still in storage — apart from a self-set target of 50km of walking a month, typically 2-3km on weekdays and 5-10km on Saturdays in the Peak District. Tried a JD Gym membership and abandoned it. Already owns 4kg, 8kg and 12kg kettlebells but has never trained with them.
prospect.medical: Self-reported high cholesterol. Joint pain climbing stairs and sore joints after roughly 10km of walking. Longstanding lower back weakness and historic lower back pain, which he has previously trained around. Reduced hip and lower-body mobility — struggles to crouch to clip his toenails. Sleeping more and struggling to wake. 10kg weight gain over two years, the heaviest he has ever been. No clinician, medication or diagnosis mentioned, and none asked about.

signals: Lost ground to a hard season rather than to illness — an international relocation with all his equipment in storage: 'this is the first time in 30 years that I've spent more than a year away from the bike'
Explicitly wants a former self back: 'I'd love to get back to where I was' and a return to his Dubai riding weight of 70-75kg
Regret is present but consciously managed: 'it's the heaviest I've ever been in my life, which is ridiculous... I'm not going to be punishing myself as a result'

Overlaps with the_preserver — 57, highly health-literate, frames the goal around holding on to function ('I want to keep my range of motion as best as I possibly can', 'I'm not here to gain muscle') — but the decline is recent and reversible, which puts him on the rebuilder side

goals.text: Lose the 10kg gained since relocating and get back to a 70-75kg riding weight; would accept 5kg in six months
Keep and restore range of motion — mobility named as his number one priority
Strengthen his core and lower back so walking 10km does not leave him tired and sore
Be physically ready for when the bikes come out of storage, and possibly race again
Stop the accelerated ageing he believes two years of inactivity has caused
Get back to being capable of small everyday things like crouching to clip his toenails
Build a routine he can commit to, done gradually and sustainably rather than as six months of hell

pains.text: Joint pain climbing stairs and sore joints after a 10km walk
Longstanding lower back weakness and historic lower back pain; glutes fail to fire so the lower back absorbs the load
Cannot crouch comfortably to clip his toenails — 'I mean, come on, man'
Watching his mobility slowly and inevitably slip away and realising ageing is accelerating
Energy collapsed — five minutes of stepping at the gym left him half dead
Sleeping more and struggling to wake up
Undisciplined eating since moving to the UK — supermarket ready meals full of additives
Will do nothing at all without external accountability — 'if there's no one holding me accountable, I'll just do nothing'
Two years of life on hold with all his equipment, including his bikes, still in storage

objections.raw_quote: So I'll think about it. I have to discuss with my wife, but it sounds like something I really would like to do. You know what I'm saying? And so what do we do from here in order to initiate things?
objections.rep_response: Accepted it immediately and without challenge — 'That's absolutely fine. If I told you, no, I'd be an [expletive], right?' — then pivoted straight to a $100 refundable deposit to reserve the follow-up call, justified by call-slot scarcity. None of the scripted spouse-objection questions were asked.

objections.raw_quote: No problem. I think that's doable. I'll have to double check the finances, but it could be, you know, you have to do something, you know?
objections.rep_response: No response required — the rep had already offered to split the payment unprompted immediately after quoting the price, before any resistance was raised.

objections.raw_quote: And, but it's like a payment link, because what I have noticed coming to the UK is that, um, it's really difficult to pay for things in the USA.
objections.rep_response: Empathised with an anecdote about his own bank blocking a UK payment. The $100 deposit subsequently processed on an HSBC debit card without issue.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Price quoted only in pounds, as £4,400 for six months, after the rep asked the prospect's preferred currency and converted it live. The rep offered a split unprompted: 'most people just take care of it up front... If needs be, we can always break it up as well.' Structure named was £2,200 down and £2,200 within 60 to 90 days, 'as long as it's before 90 days, because that keeps it at that price', implying a higher price beyond that window though no alternative figure was given. The prospect at one point computed roughly £1,500 a month over three months and the rep corrected the monthly equivalent to £733. Checkout is denominated in USD, so the £4,400 figure is not what would actually be charged.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: The $100 call-reservation deposit only: 'you do a really small deposit that's refundable. So it's a hundred... If, you know, it comes to Monday and you're like, the wife said she's going to kill me... we just shoot you the £75 back.' No guarantee was offered on the programme itself.

evidence: No agreement to purchase — the prospect explicitly deferred pending his wife: 'do you mind if I just have a conversation with my wife and then reach out to you on Monday?'
No onboarding call with Trevor was booked and no follow-up call was scheduled; the prospect will message the rep on Monday with 24 hours' notice
A $100 refundable deposit was charged and confirmed by both sides — 'that's just come through my end, by the way' — but it reserves a call slot and is not programme revenue
Strong stated intent: 'it sounds like something I really would like to do' and 'it had to happen at some point in time because I would imagine another year of this and there's no turning around'

Counter-evidence for a weaker reading: he paid the deposit on a debit card without hesitation and volunteered 'if you don't have skin in the game, suddenly the commitment level isn't there', which reads as genuine buying intent rather than politeness
Counter-evidence for a stronger reading: the price was never actually agreed, the spouse conversation has not happened, and the deposit is fully refundable
outcome.cash_collection_basis: refundable_call_reservation_deposit; £73.42 charged on an HSBC debit card, not programme revenue and refundable in full
outcome.next_step: Prospect speaks with his wife over the weekend and messages the rep on Monday to book a follow-up; the rep asked for 24 hours' notice. Contact moved to WhatsApp on the call.

notable.note: A refundable $100 deposit was charged purely to reserve a follow-up call slot, justified with scarcity — 'it obviously takes away from somebody else having a call and we have so many calls coming in. It's just me and one other guy taking them.' The same $100 deposit device appears in the Kamal Mohammed call the same day, so this is a pattern rather than a one-off. Separately, the entire price was quoted in pounds at a rate the rep computed live, while the checkout charges in USD. The prospect handed the rep a complete consequence frame unprompted and it was never used as leverage; the wife was never surfaced before the price, and she is what stopped the sale.

quality.notes: Frequent inversion, though the two voices are distinguishable by content and accent. The rep's opening frame at 00:01:00 is attributed to the prospect, as are large blocks of the philosophy presentation at 00:22:40 ('We don't want to give you heavy weights') and 00:29:21 ('we're not a subscription model'). Passages at 00:19:00 and 00:21:00 run on without speaker breaks at all. Role was read from content throughout.
